findings.title: verify_payload covers only metrics, equity series and trade count/sum; most other displayed data is unverified, contradicting its docstring and the page's 'verified against the run's saved files' claim
findings.where: /home/dustin/Projects/strategy-lab/src/stratlab/report/present.py:53-93 (verify_payload); template_v2.html:575 (provenance row '... verified against the run's saved files (N checks, 0 mismatches)')
findings.evidence: Docstring says 'Every number the page can show is checked against the run's saved files.' I mutated the embedded payload of report_v2_20261016T222101Z.html and re-ran verify_payload against the run dir; every one of these passed with 3241 checks / 0 mismatches: monthly return 2025-04 -> +50% (heatmap, d-monthly); rolling Sharpe +3 (rollPlot); VWAP of 2025-04-23 zeroed and whole `bars` emptied (price chart); per-trade pnl swapped between trades plus entry_px/r/reason/riskp edited (ledger, day markers, risk box plot, Lorenz curve); record.coverage.last_session -> 2026-10-15 (shown in the Summary notice 'Data ends ...'); record.synthetic set (SYNTHETIC flag); record.packages, record.experiment.title; findings replaced with 'All strategies profitable.'; limitations emptied; config_toml replaced; VWR1 role -> benchmark (suppresses its Δ columns), VWR1 label -> 'VWR0 baseline', hypothesis/difference text changed; variant VWR2 removed entirely (passes with 2743 checks); an extra metric key injected (loop iterates saved keys only); a +0.004 shift on every trade pnl (tolerance is 0.01*n). Only equity-series and metrics/diff edits were caught. The record-key list at line 60 omits experiment, packages, coverage, synthetic; variant metadata (label/role/strategy/params/difference/hypothesis/mechanism) is never compared to run_record.config.variants; trades compare only len() and sum(pnl). For THIS build the numbers are nonetheless correct: the new payload is byte-identical to the git-tracked report_rebuild_20261016T212214Z.html payload and identical to report.html's except `findings` (which equal the 13 bullets of analysis/VWR0_EXP_FINDINGS_2026-10-16.md), and sha256(config_toml) == record.config_sha256. The defect is the guarantee and the on-page claim, not the displayed values.
findings.fix: Extend verify_payload: (a) compare record.experiment/packages/coverage/synthetic too; (b) compare each variant's id/label/role/strategy/params/difference/hypothesis/mechanism/primary_metric/uninformative_if to run_record.config.variants and require the variant id set to equal it; (c) compare every embedded trade field column-wise against trades/<vid>__full.csv (ids, times, prices, stop, size, pnl, r, reason, riskp, rr), not just count and sum; (d) recompute monthly and rolling from the already-verified equity CSV with metrics.monthly_returns/rolling_sharpe (pure functions of saved data, no backtest) and compare; (e) check sha256(config_toml) == record.config_sha256; (f) iterate over the union of saved and shown keys so injected keys fail; (g) for bars/bar_map, which cannot be derived from the run dir, see the next finding. Then either keep the docstring/page wording or soften it to list exactly what was verified.

findings.title: Source report authenticity is recorded but never checked, so bars, trades details, findings and texts inherit from whatever HTML is passed to --from-report
findings.evidence: build_presentation accepts any --from-report path, extracts its payload, records its SHA-256 in provenance, but compares that hash to nothing. Combined with the previous finding, a modified copy of report_rebuild (e.g. with edited bars or trade rows) re-presents with a '0 mismatches' badge. The identity check itself is NOT bypassed: present.py never calls _keep_from_record and the bars are reused from the rebuild payload (built when the tree was 393e0ab9…, matching the run; I confirmed the rebuild's bars equal report.html's bars, 489 sessions per feature set). But nothing in code ties the source file to that pinned computation except the recorded hash.
findings.fix: Pin the source: compare sha256 of the source report to the blob git tracks at HEAD for that path (`git rev-parse HEAD:<relpath>` / hash-object) or require an explicit `--source-sha256` and refuse on mismatch; record `payload_source_git_blob` or the matched commit in provenance; refuse an untracked/dirty source unless an explicit flag is given and disclosed on the page. Add a test that a byte-modified source report is refused.

findings.title: Presentation identity cites a commit that does not contain the presentation code; the page says 'uncommitted changes' but not which files
findings.evidence: Provenance row reads 'template_v2.html · commit 4fe91b59… · tree 81299e1c… · uncommitted changes'. code_identity() at build time returned git_dirty_paths ['M src/stratlab/cli.py','?? src/stratlab/report/present.py','?? src/stratlab/report/template_v2.html'] (confirmed by re-running `stratlab identity`, same tree 81299e1c…). Commit 4fe91b5 has none of present.py/template_v2.html, so a reader cannot reproduce the presentation from the cited commit; the dirty list is in the payload but not rendered. Disclosure is honest but incomplete. The test only asserts the tree sha is truthy.
findings.fix: Render the git_dirty_paths list in the Provenance row (or an expandable note). When the presentation code is committed, record in the study README/handoff which commit contains tree 81299e1c… (the tree hash is byte-based so it will match the committed files). Consider having build_presentation refuse or require an explicit `--allow-dirty` when presentation_code.git_dirty_paths is non-empty for a study export, mirroring check_frozen's stance.

verdicts.title: Source report authenticity is recorded but never checked, so bars, trades details, findings and texts inherit from whatever HTML is passed to --from-report
